text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"The observed QA accuracy drop after storing >40 items (562412ff) is caused by token‑budget overflow inherent to naïve append strategies, and can be eliminated by adopting a rewrite/compression memory scheme similar to MemGPT’s virtual context paging (a962f389), which the rewrite‑vs‑append ablation already shows improves F1 scores while staying within budget (ad2ef3b4).","confidence":0.78,"support_ids":["562412ff","ad2ef3b4","a962f389"],"tags":["memory_overflow","rewrite_vs_append","MemGPT"]},{"statement":"Periodic consolidation (compression) of stored facts, as described in the consolidation paper (72ccf918), should further boost performance of lifelong‑memory agents (f7b5be16) by reducing cross‑fact interference and token usage, explaining why rewrite‑based memory outperforms naïve append in the ablation study (ad2ef3b4).","confidence":0.65,"support_ids":["72ccf918","f7b5be16","ad2ef3b4"],"tags":["consolidation","lifelong_memory","interference_reduction"]}]}
